title: Gmail AI assistant: Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini in your inbox
h1: a gmail assistant that sorts, drafts and briefs you
description: Connect Gmail to a bot in Metal running on Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini. What it can really do in your inbox, what it asks first, and three routines to copy.
answer: connect gmail once and a bot reads your mail, files it and writes replies in your voice. it drafts on its own. it never sends unless you tap allow. you pick the ai behind it: claude, chatgpt, gemini, whatever you already use. a routine can hand you the three emails that matter before your coffee's done.

review.by: lead agent, against Metal docs and the composio gmail catalog

og_line: what a bot can really do in your inbox.

app.name: Gmail
app.intro: **it works your inbox the way you would.** search, open the thread, label it, write the reply, leave it in drafts. these are the actions that do the real work.

highlight.use: search with gmail's own words, like `from:acme newer_than:7d` or `is:unread`
read a whole conversation before answering it, not just the last reply
open the invoice or contract a message carries
file mail under labels like `needs me` or `receipts`
write a reply and leave it in drafts for you to read
fix a draft when you say "shorter" or "warmer"
send, only after you tap **Allow** (or within a daily amount you set)
clear out what you told it to clear; tell it to check with you first

app.setup:
**more than one inbox? fine.** connect each gmail account with a label like `work` or `personal`, then tell the bot which one you mean. up to five accounts per app.

on [dusk cloud](/docs/dusk-cloud) the connection is included. on your own computer it goes through Metal's own connection service, so there's no key to set up.

routines_intro: **send one of these and it runs from then on.** change the times and the words. that's the whole setup.

routines.name: morning inbox brief
routines.message: every weekday at 8, read what came into my gmail since yesterday evening. tell me the 3 to 5 things that need me today, one line each, with who it's from. skip newsletters and receipts. don't reply to anything.
routines.output: a short list in your chat, nothing changed in gmail

routines.name: draft replies to clients
routines.message: whenever an email arrives from anyone at @acme.com, read the whole thread and draft a reply in my voice: short, friendly, no exclamation marks. leave it in drafts and tell me it's there. never send it yourself.
routines.when: when a matching email arrives (checked about every 15 minutes)
routines.output: a draft in gmail and a one-line note in your chat

routines.name: friday receipts sweep
routines.message: every friday at 4, find this week's receipts and invoices in gmail, add the label receipts to each, and give me a table of sender, amount and date. if an amount is over $500, put it at the top.
routines.output: labelled emails and a table in your chat

asks:
**reading and drafting just happen. sending waits for you.** anything that leaves your outbox (send, reply, forward) stops at a card with **Allow** and **Deny**, in the app, on your phone or in a call.

- want it to send a few on its own? set a daily amount, per bot.
- careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.
- want it hands-off entirely? allow gmail for that bot as read only. Metal blocks every change before it reaches google.

your google password never reaches a bot. you sign in on google's own page, composio holds the connection, and **Disconnect** removes it there too.
cannot: set filters, your vacation reply, imap, pop, forwarding or send-as. the standard connection doesn't get those google permissions. the bot tells you instead of retrying. your own composio project can add them.
work while your laptop sleeps. on your own computer, routines pause when it's asleep or Metal is closed. a run missed by less than 12 hours runs once when you're back. dusk cloud doesn't sleep.
jump the second mail lands. gmail is checked about every 15 minutes, so "when an email arrives" can take that long.
read more than five gmail accounts, or one you connected somewhere else. connect each one from Metal.
unsend. once you tap allow, it's gone, same as when you send it yourself.

sections.md:
**any of them. you choose per bot.** Metal has no model of its own. sign in to claude, chatgpt, gemini or grok, use an api key, or run a model on your own machine.

so "claude for gmail" and "chatgpt for gmail" are the same setup here. connect gmail once, pick the ai in the bot's model picker, swap any time. chats and memory stay put.

what you say to the bot goes from your machine to that ai, on your plan with them. not through us.

**tell it once. it remembers.** "i sign off with just my first name." "dana approves anything over $500." "never reply to recruiters."

those become notes you can read and edit under the bot's **Memory**. a week of small fixes ("shorter", "skip newsletters") and most people stop editing the drafts at all.

faq.q: can it work with two gmail accounts?
faq.a: yes. connect each one with its own label, like `work` and `personal`, and say which you mean: "brief me on work mail only". up to five accounts per app.

faq.q: will it send email without asking me?
faq.a: not unless you let it. sending asks first by default. you can set a daily amount a bot may send on its own, per bot, and change it back at any time.
the bot reads it to do the job, on the machine your bots run on, and the text goes to the ai you picked. Metal's account never sees your messages. see [privacy and your data](/docs/privacy-and-data).

the app is free for personal use on your own computer. the ai is billed by your ai provider on your plan with them. if you want routines to run while your laptop is shut, [dusk cloud](/pricing) starts at $20 a month.

steps: open **Connected apps** and sign in to gmail on google's page
make a bot and give it one job: your inbox
send it the morning brief routine below
read tomorrow's brief and tell it what to cut

worked.before:
47 unread
- 3 newsletters, 9 receipts, 22 notifications
- dana: q3 quote, by thursday?
- lee: invoice 1042 is wrong
- 10 more you'd have to open to judge
worked.after:
3 need you today
1. dana (acme): q3 quote, by thursday. draft ready.
2. lee (acme): invoice 1042 has the wrong total. draft with the fixed pdf.
3. your bank: card ends next month. no reply needed.

filed: 22 read later, 9 receipts. nothing sent.

saves.estimate: about 1 hour 40 minutes a week, if your inbox looks like the example
saves.formula:
25 minutes sorting mail each morning
- 5 minutes reading the bot's brief
= 20 minutes saved a day
x 5 workdays = 100 minutes a week
assumptions: your morning sort takes about 25 minutes now
you still read every draft before it goes
the first week of corrections isn't counted

mistakes.mistake: giving the inbox bot every app
mistakes.fix: it only needs gmail. keep your files and slack out of its reach.

mistakes.mistake: letting it send in week one
mistakes.fix: keep sending on **Ask every time** until the drafts sound like you.

mistakes.mistake: a routine with no quiet rule
mistakes.fix: add "if nothing needs me, say so in one line" or it'll pad the brief.

tip.text: start read only for a day. if the brief is right, then let it label and draft.
